clue.text: Philosopher gives king a set of new books

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
NT, the New Testament, is the set of books added to the Bible after the Old

explanation.surface: A thinker hands the monarch a fresh batch of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of new books' looks like a gift of novels but is the New Testament, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was an eighteenth-century German thinker, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Bound to be money-grubbing when getting rid of article

indicators.note: getting rid of tells us to drop the article's letter from the word for money-grubbing

parts.note: sparing means mean or frugal with money
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is destined to become a miser once they shed some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'destined to be', but 'Bound' alone is the definition, a leap; SPARING loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound and a spring are both a jump forward, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: She as tender soul shelters these people in the capital

indicators.note: shelters means the clue's phrase holds the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted woman gives refuge to local residents of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: EAST ENDERS are people from London's East End, the capital's traditional working-class district (and a TV soap).
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the eastern district of London are known by this name, so they are people in the British capital.

clue.text: Mowed a difficult patch of grass

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters of mowed and a are troublesome and must be worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cut a hard-to-manage lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of grass grown for hay or grazing is what this word names.

clue.text: Fellow given room about to go out for bread

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man or fellow

indicators.note: to go out signals that the letter for about leaves the word for room

parts.note: an attic is a room in the roof
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A man is offered a room just as he is about to leave, in search of a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to go out' reads as a phrase meaning 'on the point of leaving'; split it into 'about' (C) and 'to go out', the removal signal, so ATTIC loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Medicine provided when president's not well

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for president
ill means not well

explanation.surface: Treatment is given whenever the head of state falls sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet swallowed as a dose is a common form of medicine.

clue.text: It's an easy task to get on a tree

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy to do
taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbing a tree is presented as child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: CINCHONA is a South American tree whose bark gives quinine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinchona is a genus of South American evergreen trees, valued for quinine-yielding bark.

clue.text: Spectators not present in all-seater stadium?

explanation.surface: Onlookers are missing from a ground that has seats for every fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BY STANDERS: those who stand to watch have no place in a ground where everyone must sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Onlookers who watch without taking part are spectators; and people who stand are absent where every fan must be seated.

clue.text: Top star in critical phase

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words critical phase

explanation.surface: A leading performer is going through a crucial stage of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top star' suggests a celebrity, but it is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in a constellation is labelled with the first Greek letter, so it is the leading one.

clue.text: Racial identity then changing one large town

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of then are altered into a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A sense of heritage that shifts once a big town's population grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns THEN into ETHN, then add I and CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnicity means belonging to a group sharing national or cultural origins, close to racial identity.

clue.text: It's not the editor being stigmatised

parts.note: 'tain't is a dialect contraction of it ain't, meaning it is not
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone insists the newspaper editor is not the one being disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TAIN'T is folksy speech for 'it ain't', that is 'it's not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tainted is marked with disgrace, so it has been stigmatised.

clue.text: European jazz enthusiast is a beast

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
cat is jazz slang for an enthusiast or hip musician

explanation.surface: A Continental fan of jazz is described as an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' as jazz slang for a fan dates from the swing era.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred animal of the weasel family, so it is a wild beast.

clue.text: Enjoy the food with girl — drink too

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Have a hearty meal with a young woman and have a drink as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To start eating heartily is an idiom that means tucking in and relishing a meal.

clue.text: Cafe Ted and men wrecked in act of vandalism

indicators.note: wrecked tells us the letters of cafe Ted and men are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A snack bar called Ted's and its staff are trashed in a destructive attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' fits the vandal story, but it signals rearranging CAFETED and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoiling a surface, such as by graffiti, is a typical example of vandalism.

clue.text: Reduce impact of message about reservoir after drought

explanation.surface: A spokesperson softens an announcement about the dam's water levels following a dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a headline: after a drought the reservoir has its water down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute or soften a statement makes it weaker; and a dry spell leaves a reservoir with its level low.

clue.text: Opposition increases fantastically over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the shuffled letters above the next piece
fantastically means the letters of increases are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: Resistance to a policy grows remarkably as time goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges INCREASES to RESISANCE order, with T set in after; as a down clue, 'over' puts the anagram above T.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance means refusal to accept, the same sense as opposition to a plan.

clue.text: A series of degrees of little use to modern science

definitions.text: A series of degrees of little use to modern science

parts.words: A series of degrees of little use to modern science
parts.note: a series of degrees sounds like university qualifications, but means a temperature measuring system now replaced in the lab by Celsius

explanation.surface: A string of academic qualifications that are worthless to today's scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' suggests university qualifications; they are temperature degrees, on the scale scientists have abandoned for Celsius.
explanation.definitionFit: This temperature scale, with water freezing at 32 degrees, is largely replaced by Celsius in scientific work.

clue.text: House with male beast in native country

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A home shared with a man and an animal in the land of one's birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's homeland is the nation where they were born, their native country.

clue.text: Greeks in awful place seen suffering

parts.note: hell is a byword for an awful place

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters of seen are tormented into a new order

explanation.surface: People of Greece are spotted in torment in a dreadful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenes is the name the people of Greece use for themselves.

clue.text: Lisa comes around in night attire

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of Lisa comes are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman visits wearing her nightclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are light sleeveless women's tops, worn as lingerie or nightwear.

clue.text: Get hold of second drug to banish disease

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to cure is to get rid of an illness

explanation.surface: Obtain a further dose of medicine to drive out an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to obtain it, a synonym for get hold of.

clue.text: Saints seen over period of time as wise people

indicators.note: over tells us the saints' letters are spread across and around the period of time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Holy figures are regarded through the years as men of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sages are profoundly wise individuals, often elderly thinkers.

clue.text: Officer crossing a road that's next to house?

indicators.note: crossing means the officer's letters straddle the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for General, a senior officer

explanation.surface: An army officer crosses the street beside a dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a garden is typically beside a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The cultivated plot beside a home is the usual meaning of this word, hence the playful example.

clue.text: Girl is ungenerous type hoarding pounds

indicators.note: hoarding means the stingy person keeps the pounds stashed inside

parts.note: a meanie is a stingy person
L stands for librae, the Latin pounds behind the £ sign

explanation.surface: A young woman is a skinflint who stockpiles her money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' fits a miser, but here puts L inside MEANIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanie is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Fix slow mover not taking the lead

indicators.note: not taking the lead means the first letter of the slow creature is dropped

parts.note: a snail is proverbially slow

explanation.surface: Repair a sluggish runner that refuses to go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten or fix it in place.

clue.text: Presided over African country, suppressing anger

indicators.note: suppressing means the country holds the anger down within it

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Someone ruled an African nation while keeping their temper in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Dismal day on vessel beset by downpour?

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the day's letter above the vessel

parts.note: Noah's ark was the boat that rode out the Flood's endless rain

explanation.surface: A gloomy day aboard a boat lashed by heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a cryptic description: the vessel besieged by forty days of rain is Noah's ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark can mean gloomy or cheerless, a synonym for dismal.

clue.text: Adrian and Ben struggle with fierce animal

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters of Adrian and Ben grapple into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two men wrestle with a ferocious creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The NANDI BEAR is a legendary ferocious beast said to roam Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: This cryptid of East African folklore is reputed to be savage, so it is a fierce animal.

clue.text: Obvious vehicle for the French to get into

indicators.note: to get into tells us the French article goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
le is French for the

explanation.surface: It is plain which car the French should climb into.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear means plain to see, a synonym for obvious.
